purpose: Non-Mundarica discovery and exact-locator audit for a peer-reviewed Mundari speech-technology paper. The immutable WEB-MUN observation is retained, but deterministic DOI/title/author reconciliation shows that this manifestation is already represented by SRC-MMSC-000012 and therefore must not inflate unique or unresolved source counts.

records.title: MunTTS: A Text-to-Speech System for Mundari
records.venue: Proceedings of the Seventh Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL 2024)
records.rights_note: The proceedings PDF identifies copyright 2024 Association for Computational Linguistics. This run does not infer a broader licence from public readability. No participant-derived audio, transcripts, speaker identifiers, or Karya corpus files are ingested solely from the paper.
records.scope_note: Directly relevant to Mundari language technology and dataset provenance. The paper reports work on Jharkhand Mundari written in Devanagari, source-text translation/validation, speaker selection, studio recording, corpus composition, train/dev/test split and native-speaker evaluation. These are paper-attributed methodological facts, not community-wide cultural claims.

canonicalization.decision: Preserve WEB-MUN-0090 as an immutable later audit observation of the same MunTTS paper already registered as SRC-MMSC-000012. Do not increase audited-identity, unique-lead, canonicalized-new-identity or unresolved-lead counts.
